site.name: 使用说明书
site.description: wunder is an agent orchestration platform: Pupa (desktop) is the local AI workbench, Beehive (web) is the cloud AI workbench, Helm (cli) is the manual local entry point, and the Hull (server) is the user and agent management platform. / wunder 是一个智能体调度平台：蛹（desktop）是本地 AI 工作台，蜂巢（web）是云端 AI 工作台，舵机（cli）是手工本地操作入口，舰体（server）是用户与智能体管理平台。

pages.title: wunder 心舰
pages.summary: wunder 是智能体调度平台。蛹是电脑上的本地 AI 工作台，蜂巢是浏览器里的云端工作台，舵机是终端入口，舰体是多人共用的管理平台。

pages.title: 快速开始
pages.summary: 用最短路径把蛹跑起来：下载、启动、配模型、发第一条消息、验证结果。个人用户默认入口，无需部署服务。

pages.title: 蛹（desktop）入门
pages.summary: wunder 的默认使用方式：本地 AI 工作台。下载安装即可使用，不需要先部署舰体；同进程原生调用引擎，不占端口，不走 HTTP/WebSocket 中转。

pages.title: 形态矩阵
pages.summary: 各程序形态的技术栈、定位、运行方式与系统支持对比，以及按场景选择形态的依据。

pages.title: 核心概览
pages.summary: wunder 为什么这样表现——四个核心（快速、稳定、通用、轻量），以及四个形态与深入主题。

pages.title: 舰体（server）部署
pages.summary: 可选形态。多人共用的用户与智能体管理平台：多租户、权限治理、渠道接入、智能体应用发布。舰体启动后同端口挂舰桥（18000），蜂巢由独立的网页服务容器下发（18001）。

pages.title: 舵机（cli）使用
pages.summary: 手工本地操作入口。终端里进交互界面，管道里自动降级为一次性执行；22 条斜杠命令、exec --json 事件流、cloud 子命令全套；舵机侧关闭定时任务与引擎排队。

pages.title: 说明书总览
pages.summary: 说明书导航页：从蛹起步，按需进入界面地图、其它形态与能力。start 与 surfaces 两组的全部页面都在这里。

pages.title: 常用说明目录
pages.summary: 仓库文档生态导航：设计文档、技术说明书、API 文档、使用说明书、性能标准与评分、功能迭代、经验教训的分工与读法。

pages.title: 首次运行排查
pages.summary: 各形态第一次启动或部署最常见的失败模式与验证点：蛹启动、舰体部署、蜂巢访问、舵机执行。

pages.title: 帮助
pages.summary: 按症状分流的帮助入口：故障排查、FAQ、术语表。

pages.title: 故障排查
pages.summary: 按症状列出常见问题的检查项。

pages.title: FAQ
pages.summary: 使用 wunder 时的常见结论与答复。

pages.title: 术语表
pages.summary: wunder 文档里的核心术语与形态名称对照。

pages.title: 工具总览
pages.summary: wunder 的内置工具矩阵，按八个分类指向对应工具文档；选型入口、结果形态约定，以及不套统一外壳的几个例外。

pages.title: 计划面板 / 问询面板 / 会话让出
pages.summary: 三个交互控制工具：维护可见的执行计划、动手前向用户征询路线、主动让出当前轮次等待外部事件。

pages.title: 工作区文件
pages.summary: 浏览工作区、搜索内容、读文件和写文件这几个最常用操作的使用方式。

pages.title: 执行命令
pages.summary: 运行 shell 命令、编译、测试或调用现成的命令行工具；支持预演、资源预算和输出守卫。

pages.title: 技能调用
pages.summary: 把一个技能的说明和目录加载进当前对话，让智能体照着技能流程干活。

pages.title: 网页抓取
pages.summary: 让智能体读取一个网页的正文，用于查资料、读文档、看接口返回。

pages.title: 浏览器工具族
pages.summary: 浏览器不是单个工具：启用后自动注册一组 `browser_*` 工具，用来打开页面、点击、输入、等待、截图和读取渲染后的内容。

pages.title: 读图工具
pages.summary: 把本地的图片、动图或视频送进当前对话，让智能体直接看这些素材。

pages.title: 多模态生成
pages.summary: 语音生成、声转文、图像生成、视频生成四个工具：适用场景、所需模型类型、产物落盘位置。

pages.title: 桌面控制
pages.summary: 桌面控制器与桌面监视器在桌面模式下操作本机鼠标键盘、截图观察，并把画面作为视觉输入追加给模型。

pages.title: 子智能体控制
pages.summary: 让主智能体把一块独立工作派给子智能体去做，并跟踪、等待、引导和回收它们。

pages.title: 会话线程控制
pages.summary: 让智能体同时推进多件事：新建、切换、改名、归档和恢复任务线程。

pages.title: 自我状态
pages.summary: 让智能体自查当前会话的模型、上下文占用、轮次进度和事件计数，用来判断要不要压缩上下文或收尾。

pages.title: 记忆管理
pages.summary: 管理当前智能体在当前用户下的长期记忆碎片：列出、搜索、读取、新增、更新、删除，以及“短索引注入 + 按需取全文”的用法。

pages.title: 定时任务
pages.summary: 让智能体按时间自动干活：创建、修改、查询、立即执行和启停定时任务。

pages.title: 扩展与动态工具
pages.summary: 工具、技能、能力、用户工具四层关系，以及 MCP、技能、知识库是怎么被动态注册和路由的。

pages.title: 界面概览
pages.summary: 四个形态对应四个界面：蛹（本地 AI 工作台）、蜂巢（云端 AI 工作台）、舵机（终端界面）、舰桥（治理后台）。按形态查界面能力。

pages.title: 蜂巢界面
pages.summary: 蜂巢是云端 AI 工作台，随舰体提供、浏览器访问。设置内含工具、记忆、渠道、定时、设备、归档；支持双向语音（含 TTS），没有交互式终端。

pages.title: 舰桥界面
pages.summary: 舰桥是舰体的治理与调试后台。顶层导航 4 组 19 项：系统 4、智能体 6、调试 6、文档 2。

pages.title: 蛹界面
pages.summary: 蛹（desktop）是本地 AI 工作台，个人用户的默认入口。主窗只有对话、设置两页，设置内 12 个分类，其余能力以面板和对话框呈现。

pages.title: 能力概览
pages.summary: 能力与操作参考概览：核心能力、功能入口、状态含义、设置项含义。

pages.title: 功能与能力速查
pages.summary: wunder 的能力清单、入口位置与相关文档。

pages.title: 目标
pages.summary: 目标核心让智能体进入目标态并持续完成一项任务：三个工具驱动、四种相位、默认 256 轮上限，连续 3 轮无进展自动受阻。

pages.title: 兼容性
pages.summary: 兼容性核心让蛹与舵机在旧操作系统环境中可运行并被明确约束：Windows 7 32 位与 Ubuntu 18.04 各有离线构建链，界面走软件渲染不依赖 GPU。

pages.title: 上下文压缩
pages.summary: 长对话不会因为太长而中断：系统在必要时精简历史、保留最有效的信息，让对话继续。

pages.title: 子智能体
pages.summary: 子智能体核心在单一线程内派生子任务，交给独立执行体完成并回传结果；协作形态只有子智能体一种，蜂群编排已从引擎与协议层移除。

pages.title: 定时任务
pages.summary: 智能体在指定时间自动执行：at 定点、every 固定间隔、cron 表达式三种排程，配租约、退避与自动禁用，进程重启不丢任务。

pages.title: 渠道
pages.summary: 飞书、QQ、微信、XMPP 和通用 webhook 各自的支持范围，以及消息到智能体与工作区的绑定解析。

pages.title: 记忆
pages.summary: 长期资料在线程创建时注入一次，之后保持冻结。它的两层结构，以及使用上的注意点。

pages.title: 多线程
pages.summary: 多线程核心在单进程内通过并发控制提升吞吐与资源利用：单用户可并发多任务线程，配会话队列、会话锁、并行度上限与日配额。

pages.title: 多用户管理
pages.summary: 舰体形态下的用户、单位与权限边界：登录态、在线状态、单位树、等级与额度、智能体定义文档和数据隔离。

pages.title: 三端互通
pages.summary: 蜂巢、蛹、舵机在同一账号下统一在线状态、跨端工作区互见并双向远程控制。

pages.title: 系统架构
pages.summary: 四个形态共用同一套核心与引擎，真正的执行发生在会话里，界面读到的是一份有界的展示视图。

pages.title: 智能体循环
pages.summary: 你只说一次目标，剩下的步骤引擎替你跑：循环按模型轮次推进，到终态或刹车为止。

pages.title: 工具
pages.summary: 智能体做事的能力来自四层结构——执行体工具、可调用知识与脚本的技能、管理员选择的能力、用户自己接入的工具；四层不是一回事，「能选」不等于「能调」。

pages.title: 工具体系
pages.summary: 工具从注册、被选中、分发到结果落地的完整链路，以及并行度、超时、预算和裁剪口径。

pages.title: 实时性
pages.summary: 执行过程持续可见：WebSocket 是唯一实时通道，断线用游标补水补齐，客户端看到的始终是后端真相的投影，慢客户端会被保护性脱钩。

pages.title: 稳定性
pages.summary: 出错不扩散、失败能恢复、问题可复盘。稳定性来自四类硬约束——有界、预算、熔断、单写者——以及出错后统一的错误结构与清楚的处置动作。

pages.title: 可观测性
pages.summary: 日志、运行时指标、监控与线程轨迹、性能与压测四类入口各自的覆盖范围，以及从错误信息出发的排障顺序。

pages.title: 工作区与工作目录
pages.summary: 每个用户有且只有一个工作区，工具以它为根；蛹里是本机上的持久目录，舰体部署时是服务端按用户划分的唯一目录。

pages.title: 会话与轮次
pages.summary: 对话的编号方式：线程、用户轮次、模型轮次、时间线条目，以及权威的计数口径。

pages.title: 流式执行
pages.summary: 执行过程实时到达界面的路径：先落库再推送、按游标续传、前端只消费有界视图。

pages.title: 运行时与在线状态
pages.summary: 会话不只是静态历史，还带着运行时状态：正在执行、等待审批、等一个输入……这些状态表示会话当前在做什么。

pages.title: 提示词与技能
pages.summary: 系统提示词决定智能体的"人格"，技能是它在某类任务里的具体做法。

pages.title: 长期记忆
pages.summary: 智能体「记住」你的偏好、背景和长期资料：结构化记忆在对话开始时注入一次，运行中按需补充检索。

pages.title: 额度与 Token 用量
pages.summary: 每次模型请求消耗 1 额度，每天发放 1000；Token 用量只用于观测，不参与扣减。

pages.title: 目标态
pages.summary: 目标态是按模型轮次预算驱动的会话级持久目标：设定一次，智能体就自动接着做，直到完成、受阻或预算用尽。

pages.title: 形象系统
pages.summary: 形象是挂在智能体上的视觉陪伴层：ZIP 形象包 + 精灵表动画，跟着运行状态换动画行，不参与任何执行逻辑。

pages.title: 边界处理
pages.summary: 上下文超限、网络中断、工具失败、任务排队：系统在这些边界情况下保持稳定，而不是直接崩溃。

pages.title: 会话状态说明
pages.summary: 会话状态、审批状态、异常状态与连接状态的含义及处理方式。

pages.title: 提示词与个性化
pages.summary: 定制智能体的角色定位和回答风格：选内置模板，或自己写一套。

pages.title: 系统设置参考
pages.summary: 常用设置项的含义、推荐值与生效规则。

pages.title: 工作区路由与文件管理
pages.summary: 每个用户的工作区只有一个云端目录，路径一律是工作区相对路径；容器参数已收敛，不再按智能体或容器派生根。

pages.title: 舰桥面板指南
pages.summary: 舰桥各面板的职能、入口位置与常用操作流程。

pages.title: 微信 iLink 渠道
pages.summary: 新微信渠道用 iLink 协议，跟旧的公众号、企业微信不是一套。

pages.title: 聊天 WebSocket
pages.summary: 聊天的实时通道，同时也是会话控制通道：启动执行、断线续传、观察、取消、回传审批都在同一条连接上。

pages.title: MCP 入口
pages.summary: wunder 既能把自己作为 MCP 服务暴露出去，也能作为 MCP 客户端接入外部服务。

pages.title: wunder
pages.summary: wunder is an agent orchestration platform. The Pupa is the local AI workbench on your computer, the Beehive is the cloud workbench in a browser, the Helm is the terminal entry point, and the Hull is the shared management platform for teams.

pages.title: Quick Start
pages.summary: The shortest path to get the Pupa running: download, launch, configure a model, send your first message, verify the result. The default entry point for individual users, with no service to deploy.

pages.title: Starting with the Pupa (Desktop)
pages.summary: wunder's default way to work: a local AI workbench. Download, install, open, go — no Hull to deploy first; it calls the engine natively in-process, takes no port, and routes through no HTTP/WebSocket relay.

pages.title: Form matrix
pages.summary: How the program forms compare on tech stack, purpose, run model and OS support, plus which form to pick for your scenario.

pages.title: Core Concepts
pages.summary: Why wunder behaves the way it does—the four cores (fast, stable, general, lightweight), along with the four forms and the deep dives.

pages.title: Deploying the Hull (Server)
pages.summary: An optional form. The user-and-agent management platform for multi-user sharing: multi-tenancy, permission governance, channel integration, and agent-app publishing. Once the Hull is up, the Bridge (18000) is served on the same port, and the Beehive is delivered by a separate web-service container (18001).

pages.title: Using the Helm (CLI)
pages.summary: The manual local entry point. In a terminal it opens an interactive session; in a pipeline it degrades to a one-shot run. The full set of 22 slash commands, an exec --json event stream, and the complete cloud subcommand family; scheduled tasks and engine queueing are off on the Helm.

pages.title: Manual Overview
pages.summary: The manual's navigation page: start from the Pupa and move into the interface map, other forms, and capabilities as needed. Every page in the start and surfaces groups is here.

pages.title: Documentation Directory
pages.summary: A guide to the repo's documentation ecosystem: how the overview and design docs, technical manual, API reference, user manual, performance standards and scoring, changelog, and lessons-learned divide the work, and how to read them.

pages.title: First-Run Troubleshooting
pages.summary: The most common failure modes and verification points for the first launch or deployment of each form: Pupa startup, Hull deployment, Beehive access, Helm execution. When the first run doesn't work, locate the failure by form here.

pages.title: Help
pages.summary: Entry page for locating a problem by symptom.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.summary: Cause and check points by symptom.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.summary: Common conclusions for using wunder, ahead of symptom-level troubleshooting.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.summary: Core terms in wunder documentation, explained in plain language.

pages.title: Tools Overview
pages.summary: wunder's built-in tool matrix, eight categories pointing at the matching tool pages, plus selection entry points by situation, the conventions for how results are shaped, and a few exceptions that skip the shared shell.

pages.title: Plan Panel / Question Panel / Sessions Yield
pages.summary: Three interaction-control tools: maintaining a visible execution plan, asking the user for a route before acting, and yielding the current turn to wait for an external event.

pages.title: Workspace Files
pages.summary: Browsing the workspace, searching content, reading files, and writing files.

pages.title: Execute Command
pages.summary: Run shell commands, compile, test, or call an existing command-line tool; it supports previews, resource budgets, and output guards.

pages.title: Skill Call
pages.summary: Loading a skill's instructions and its directory into the current conversation so the agent can work through that skill's process.

pages.title: Web Fetch
pages.summary: Letting the agent read the body of a web page, for looking things up, reading docs, or inspecting API responses.

pages.title: Browser Tools
pages.summary: The browser is not a single tool: once enabled it registers a group of `browser_*` tools for opening pages, clicking, typing, waiting, taking screenshots, and reading rendered content.

pages.title: Desktop Control
pages.summary: In desktop mode, the Desktop Controller and Desktop Monitor drive the local mouse and keyboard, capture screenshots, and feed the picture to the model as appended visual input.

pages.title: Read Image
pages.summary: Send a local image, animated GIF, or video into the current conversation so the agent can look at the material directly.

pages.title: Subagent Control
pages.summary: Letting the main agent hand a self-contained piece of work to subagents, then track, wait on, guide, and reclaim them.

pages.title: Thread Control
pages.summary: Letting the agent move several things forward at once: create, switch, rename, archive, and restore task threads.

pages.title: Self Status
pages.summary: Checks the current session's model, context usage, round progress, and event counts, for deciding whether to compress context or wrap up.

pages.title: Memory Manager
pages.summary: Manage the current agent's long-term memory fragments under the current user: list, search, read, add, update, and remove, along with the "short index injection plus fetch-on-demand" pattern.

pages.title: Schedule Task
pages.summary: Creates, changes, inspects, runs right away, and enables or disables scheduled jobs.

pages.title: Interface Overview
pages.summary: Four forms, four interfaces — the Pupa (local AI workbench), the Beehive (cloud AI workbench), the Helm (terminal interface), and the Bridge (admin governance console). Look up interface capabilities by form.

pages.title: Beehive Interface
pages.summary: The Beehive is the cloud AI workbench, provided with the Hull deployment and reached in a browser. Its settings include tools, memory, channels, scheduled tasks, devices, and archive; it supports two-way voice (TTS included) and has no interactive terminal.

pages.title: Bridge Interface
pages.summary: The Bridge is the Hull's governance and debugging console. Its top-level navigation has 4 groups and 19 items: System 4, Agents 6, Debug 6, Docs 2.

pages.title: Pupa Interface
pages.summary: The Pupa (desktop) is the local AI workbench and the default entry for individual users. Its main window has only two pages, chat and settings, with 12 categories in settings; everything else appears as panels and dialogs.

pages.title: Capabilities Overview
pages.summary: Capabilities and operating references: the core capabilities, where a feature lives, what a status means, and how to change a setting.

pages.title: Feature and Capability Quick Reference
pages.summary: What wunder can do and where each capability lives, organized by feature area.

pages.title: Goal
pages.summary: The Goal core lets an agent enter goal mode and keep working on one task: three tools drive it, four phases, a default 256-round cap, and automatic blocking after 3 consecutive rounds without progress.

pages.title: Compatibility
pages.summary: The Compatibility core lets the Pupa (desktop) and the Helm (cli) run in older operating-system environments under explicit constraints: Windows 7 32-bit and Ubuntu 18.04 each have an offline build chain, and the interface uses software rendering that does not depend on a GPU.

pages.title: Context Compression
pages.summary: Long conversations are not cut short when they grow long. The system trims history in graded levels, keeps the most useful information, and lets the conversation continue.

pages.title: Subagents
pages.summary: The Subagents core forks a subtask inside a single thread for an independent executor to complete and return to the parent; the only collaborative form is the subagent, and swarm orchestration has been removed from the engine and the protocol layer.

pages.title: Scheduled Tasks
pages.summary: Scheduled tasks run the agent at a chosen time: three schedule kinds — at for a one-off point, every for a fixed interval, cron for a recurring pattern — with leases, backoff, and auto-disable, so tasks survive a process restart.

pages.title: Channels
pages.summary: Feishu, QQ, WeChat, XMPP, and generic webhooks differ in support level; an inbound message is routed to its agent and workspace by binding.

pages.title: Memory
pages.summary: Long-term data is injected once when a thread is created and stays frozen afterwards; it has two layers, initialization injection and runtime recall.

pages.title: Multi-threading
pages.summary: The Multi-threading core raises throughput and resource use through concurrency control inside a single process: one user can hold several concurrent task threads, backed by a session queue, session locks, a parallelism cap, and a daily quota.

pages.title: Multi-user Management
pages.summary: Users, units, and permission boundaries in the Hull (server) form — login state, presence, the unit tree, levels and credits, agent definition documents, and data isolation.

pages.title: Interlink
pages.summary: The Beehive, the Pupa, and the Helm share one presence state, see each other's workspaces, and control each other in both directions.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: All four forms share the same core and engine; real execution happens inside sessions, and the interface reads a bounded display view.

pages.title: Agent Loop
pages.summary: You state the goal once and the engine runs the remaining steps; the loop advances round by round until it reaches a deliverable result or hits a brake.

pages.title: Tools
pages.summary: The agent's ability to act comes from a four-layer structure: executor tools, skills that package callable knowledge and scripts, capabilities the administrator selects, and tools the user connects. Keeping the layers distinct is what keeps "selectable" separate from "invokable".

pages.title: Tool System
pages.summary: The full path a tool takes from registration and selection through dispatch to its result landing, along with parallelism, timeouts, budgets, and clipping conventions.

pages.title: Realtime
pages.summary: The realtime channel runs on WebSocket; a reconnect catches up by cursor; what the client sees is a projection of backend truth; slow clients are uncoupled to protect the stream.

pages.title: Stability
pages.summary: Errors that do not spread, failures that can recover, and problems that can be reviewed. Stability comes from four kinds of hard constraint — bounds, budgets, circuit breaking, and a single writer — plus a consistent error structure and clear actions when something goes wrong.

pages.title: Observability
pages.summary: Where to start looking when something breaks — what logs, runtime metrics and alerts, monitoring and thread traces, and performance testing each tell you, and the order to work through a failure from the error message onward.

pages.title: Workspaces and the Working Directory
pages.summary: Each user has exactly one workspace, and tools are rooted at it: a persistent local directory in the Pupa, or a single per-user directory on the server in a Hull deployment.

pages.title: Sessions and Rounds
pages.summary: How a conversation is numbered: threads, user rounds, model rounds, timeline entries, and the authoritative counting conventions.

pages.title: Streaming Execution
pages.summary: Events are persisted before they are pushed, a reconnect resumes by cursor, and the frontend consumes bounded views.

pages.title: Runtime and Online Status
pages.summary: A conversation is not just static history: it also carries runtime state such as running, waiting for approval, or waiting for input, and that state tells you what the session is doing right now.

pages.title: Prompts and Skills
pages.summary: The system prompt shapes the agent's persona, and skills are its operating manuals for a class of task.

pages.title: Long-term Memory
pages.summary: How the agent "remembers" your preferences, background, and long-term material—structured memory is injected once when a conversation starts, then supplemented by recall as it runs.

pages.title: Quota and Token Usage
pages.summary: Each model request costs 1 credit and 1000 are granted daily; token usage is observed only and never deducted.

pages.title: Goal Mode
pages.summary: Goal mode is a session-level persistent goal driven by a model-round budget — set it once, and the agent keeps going on its own until it completes, gets blocked, or spends the budget.

pages.title: Companion System
pages.summary: A companion is a visual layer attached to an agent — a ZIP companion package plus a sprite sheet that follows the runtime state and takes no part in any execution logic.

pages.title: Boundary Handling
pages.summary: Context overflow, network interruption, tool failure, queued tasks — the system stays stable under these boundary conditions instead of crashing outright.

pages.title: Session Status Guide
pages.summary: What the various statuses in a chat mean, what the agent is doing, and what to do when something goes wrong.

pages.title: Prompts and Personalization
pages.summary: Customize the agent's role and answer style — pick a built-in template, or write your own.

pages.title: System Settings Reference
pages.summary: What the common settings mean and what to set them to.

pages.title: Workspace Routing and File Management
pages.summary: Each user has a single cloud workspace directory. Paths are always workspace-relative, and the container parameter has been converged — directories are no longer derived per agent or container.

pages.title: Bridge Panel Guide
pages.summary: What each panel in the Bridge manages and where its entry lives.

pages.title: WeChat iLink Channel
pages.summary: The new WeChat channel uses the iLink protocol and is not the same thing as the legacy Official Account or WeCom channels.

pages.title: Chat WebSocket
pages.summary: The real-time channel for chat and also the session control channel: starting an execution, resuming after a disconnect, watching, canceling, and returning approvals all happen on the same connection.

pages.title: MCP Endpoint
pages.summary: wunder can both expose itself as an MCP service and act as an MCP client to connect to external services.

zh-CN/index.title: wunder 心舰
zh-CN/index.summary: wunder 是智能体调度平台。蛹是电脑上的本地 AI 工作台，蜂巢是浏览器里的云端工作台，舵机是终端入口，舰体是多人共用的管理平台。

headings.text: 四个形态，按场景选一个
一个智能体，多个任务并行

zh-CN/start/quickstart.title: 快速开始
zh-CN/start/quickstart.summary: 用最短路径把蛹跑起来：下载、启动、配模型、发第一条消息、验证结果。个人用户默认入口，无需部署服务。

zh-CN/start/desktop.title: 蛹（desktop）入门
zh-CN/start/desktop.summary: wunder 的默认使用方式：本地 AI 工作台。下载安装即可使用，不需要先部署舰体；同进程原生调用引擎，不占端口，不走 HTTP/WebSocket 中转。

headings.text: 界面结构（主窗只有两页）
蛹独有能力（其他界面没有）

zh-CN/start/forms.title: 形态矩阵
zh-CN/start/forms.summary: 各程序形态的技术栈、定位、运行方式与系统支持对比，以及按场景选择形态的依据。

zh-CN/concepts/index.title: 核心概览
zh-CN/concepts/index.summary: wunder 为什么这样表现——四个核心（快速、稳定、通用、轻量），以及四个形态与深入主题。

zh-CN/start/server.title: 舰体（server）部署
zh-CN/start/server.summary: 可选形态。多人共用的用户与智能体管理平台：多租户、权限治理、渠道接入、智能体应用发布。舰体启动后同端口挂舰桥（18000），蜂巢由独立的网页服务容器下发（18001）。

zh-CN/start/cli.title: 舵机（cli）使用
zh-CN/start/cli.summary: 手工本地操作入口。终端里进交互界面，管道里自动降级为一次性执行；22 条斜杠命令、exec --json 事件流、cloud 子命令全套；舵机侧关闭定时任务与引擎排队。

headings.text: 舵机独有能力（其他界面没有）

zh-CN/start/hubs.title: 说明书总览
zh-CN/start/hubs.summary: 说明书导航页：从蛹起步，按需进入界面地图、其它形态与能力。start 与 surfaces 两组的全部页面都在这里。

zh-CN/start/docs-directory.title: 常用说明目录
zh-CN/start/docs-directory.summary: 仓库文档生态导航：设计文档、技术说明书、API 文档、使用说明书、性能标准与评分、功能迭代、经验教训的分工与读法。

headings.text: 技术说明书（docs/技术说明书/）

zh-CN/start/troubleshooting-first-run.title: 首次运行排查
zh-CN/start/troubleshooting-first-run.summary: 各形态第一次启动或部署最常见的失败模式与验证点：蛹启动、舰体部署、蜂巢访问、舵机执行。

zh-CN/help/index.title: 帮助
zh-CN/help/index.summary: 按症状分流的帮助入口：故障排查、FAQ、术语表。

zh-CN/help/troubleshooting.title: 故障排查
zh-CN/help/troubleshooting.summary: 按症状列出常见问题的检查项。

zh-CN/help/faq.title: FAQ
zh-CN/help/faq.summary: 使用 wunder 时的常见结论与答复。

webfetch 与浏览器工具的区别

zh-CN/help/glossary.title: 术语表
zh-CN/help/glossary.summary: wunder 文档里的核心术语与形态名称对照。

zh-CN/tools/index.title: 工具总览
zh-CN/tools/index.summary: wunder 的内置工具矩阵，按八个分类指向对应工具文档；选型入口、结果形态约定，以及不套统一外壳的几个例外。

headings.text: 只有关键词，想找网页来源
要点击、输入、等页面动态渲染

zh-CN/tools/panels.title: 计划面板 / 问询面板 / 会话让出
zh-CN/tools/panels.summary: 三个交互控制工具：维护可见的执行计划、动手前向用户征询路线、主动让出当前轮次等待外部事件。

headings.text: 计划面板 / 问询面板 / 会话让出

zh-CN/tools/workspace-files.title: 工作区文件
zh-CN/tools/workspace-files.summary: 浏览工作区、搜索内容、读文件和写文件这几个最常用操作的使用方式。

zh-CN/tools/exec.title: 执行命令
zh-CN/tools/exec.summary: 运行 shell 命令、编译、测试或调用现成的命令行工具；支持预演、资源预算和输出守卫。

zh-CN/tools/skill-call.title: 技能调用
zh-CN/tools/skill-call.summary: 把一个技能的说明和目录加载进当前对话，让智能体照着技能流程干活。

zh-CN/tools/web-fetch.title: 网页抓取
zh-CN/tools/web-fetch.summary: 让智能体读取一个网页的正文，用于查资料、读文档、看接口返回。

zh-CN/tools/browser.title: 浏览器工具族
zh-CN/tools/browser.summary: 浏览器不是单个工具：启用后自动注册一组 `browser_*` 工具，用来打开页面、点击、输入、等待、截图和读取渲染后的内容。

zh-CN/tools/read-image.title: 读图工具
zh-CN/tools/read-image.summary: 把本地的图片、动图或视频送进当前对话，让智能体直接看这些素材。

zh-CN/tools/multimodal-generation.title: 多模态生成
zh-CN/tools/multimodal-generation.summary: 语音生成、声转文、图像生成、视频生成四个工具：适用场景、所需模型类型、产物落盘位置。

headings.text: 需要配好对应类型的模型

zh-CN/tools/desktop-control.title: 桌面控制
zh-CN/tools/desktop-control.summary: 桌面控制器与桌面监视器在桌面模式下操作本机鼠标键盘、截图观察，并把画面作为视觉输入追加给模型。

zh-CN/tools/subagent-control.title: 子智能体控制
zh-CN/tools/subagent-control.summary: 让主智能体把一块独立工作派给子智能体去做，并跟踪、等待、引导和回收它们。

zh-CN/tools/thread-control.title: 会话线程控制
zh-CN/tools/thread-control.summary: 让智能体同时推进多件事：新建、切换、改名、归档和恢复任务线程。

zh-CN/tools/self-status.title: 自我状态
zh-CN/tools/self-status.summary: 让智能体自查当前会话的模型、上下文占用、轮次进度和事件计数，用来判断要不要压缩上下文或收尾。

zh-CN/tools/memory-manager.title: 记忆管理
zh-CN/tools/memory-manager.summary: 管理当前智能体在当前用户下的长期记忆碎片：列出、搜索、读取、新增、更新、删除，以及“短索引注入 + 按需取全文”的用法。

zh-CN/tools/schedule-task.title: 定时任务
zh-CN/tools/schedule-task.summary: 让智能体按时间自动干活：创建、修改、查询、立即执行和启停定时任务。

headings.text: 循环任务会不会越堆越多

zh-CN/tools/extensibility.title: 扩展与动态工具
zh-CN/tools/extensibility.summary: 工具、技能、能力、用户工具四层关系，以及 MCP、技能、知识库是怎么被动态注册和路由的。

zh-CN/surfaces/index.title: 界面概览
zh-CN/surfaces/index.summary: 四个形态对应四个界面：蛹（本地 AI 工作台）、蜂巢（云端 AI 工作台）、舵机（终端界面）、舰桥（治理后台）。按形态查界面能力。

zh-CN/surfaces/frontend.title: 蜂巢界面
zh-CN/surfaces/frontend.summary: 蜂巢是云端 AI 工作台，随舰体提供、浏览器访问。设置内含工具、记忆、渠道、定时、设备、归档；支持双向语音（含 TTS），没有交互式终端。

zh-CN/surfaces/web-admin.title: 舰桥界面
zh-CN/surfaces/web-admin.summary: 舰桥是舰体的治理与调试后台。顶层导航 4 组 19 项：系统 4、智能体 6、调试 6、文档 2。

zh-CN/surfaces/desktop-ui.title: 蛹界面
zh-CN/surfaces/desktop-ui.summary: 蛹（desktop）是本地 AI 工作台，个人用户的默认入口。主窗只有对话、设置两页，设置内 12 个分类，其余能力以面板和对话框呈现。

zh-CN/capabilities/index.title: 能力概览
zh-CN/capabilities/index.summary: 能力与操作参考概览：核心能力、功能入口、状态含义、设置项含义。

zh-CN/capabilities/api-index.title: 功能与能力速查
zh-CN/capabilities/api-index.summary: wunder 的能力清单、入口位置与相关文档。

zh-CN/concepts/core-goal.title: 目标
zh-CN/concepts/core-goal.summary: 目标核心让智能体进入目标态并持续完成一项任务：三个工具驱动、四种相位、默认 256 轮上限，连续 3 轮无进展自动受阻。

zh-CN/concepts/core-compatibility.title: 兼容性
zh-CN/concepts/core-compatibility.summary: 兼容性核心让蛹与舵机在旧操作系统环境中可运行并被明确约束：Windows 7 32 位与 Ubuntu 18.04 各有离线构建链，界面走软件渲染不依赖 GPU。

zh-CN/concepts/core-context-compression.title: 上下文压缩
zh-CN/concepts/core-context-compression.summary: 长对话不会因为太长而中断：系统在必要时精简历史、保留最有效的信息，让对话继续。

zh-CN/concepts/core-subagent.title: 子智能体
zh-CN/concepts/core-subagent.summary: 子智能体核心在单一线程内派生子任务，交给独立执行体完成并回传结果；协作形态只有子智能体一种，蜂群编排已从引擎与协议层移除。

zh-CN/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.title: 定时任务
zh-CN/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.summary: 智能体在指定时间自动执行：at 定点、every 固定间隔、cron 表达式三种排程，配租约、退避与自动禁用，进程重启不丢任务。

headings.text: 从哪里建、各形态支持情况

zh-CN/concepts/core-channels.title: 渠道
zh-CN/concepts/core-channels.summary: 飞书、QQ、微信、XMPP 和通用 webhook 各自的支持范围，以及消息到智能体与工作区的绑定解析。

headings.text: 消息怎么找到智能体和工作区
入站、出站与限流的边界

zh-CN/concepts/core-memory.title: 记忆
zh-CN/concepts/core-memory.summary: 长期资料在线程创建时注入一次，之后保持冻结。它的两层结构，以及使用上的注意点。

zh-CN/concepts/core-multithreading.title: 多线程
zh-CN/concepts/core-multithreading.summary: 多线程核心在单进程内通过并发控制提升吞吐与资源利用：单用户可并发多任务线程，配会话队列、会话锁、并行度上限与日配额。

zh-CN/concepts/core-multi-user-managemen.title: 多用户管理
zh-CN/concepts/core-multi-user-managemen.summary: 舰体形态下的用户、单位与权限边界：登录态、在线状态、单位树、等级与额度、智能体定义文档和数据隔离。

headings.text: 登录态用的是不透明令牌
单位树与负责人作用域
等级和额度是两套东西
智能体的定义文档与线程不是一回事

zh-CN/capabilities/interlink.title: 三端互通
zh-CN/capabilities/interlink.summary: 蜂巢、蛹、舵机在同一账号下统一在线状态、跨端工作区互见并双向远程控制。

zh-CN/concepts/architecture.title: 系统架构
zh-CN/concepts/architecture.summary: 四个形态共用同一套核心与引擎，真正的执行发生在会话里，界面读到的是一份有界的展示视图。

headings.text: 四个形态，界面各管各的交付
界面看到的是有界视图，不是执行快照

zh-CN/concepts/core-agent-loop.title: 智能体循环
zh-CN/concepts/core-agent-loop.summary: 你只说一次目标，剩下的步骤引擎替你跑：循环按模型轮次推进，到终态或刹车为止。

headings.text: 什么时候会自己停下来
该等、该插手、该换新线程

zh-CN/concepts/core-tools.title: 工具
zh-CN/concepts/core-tools.summary: 智能体做事的能力来自四层结构——执行体工具、可调用知识与脚本的技能、管理员选择的能力、用户自己接入的工具；四层不是一回事，「能选」不等于「能调」。

headings.text: 动态注册：模型能看到的工具不止内置清单
结果的裁剪有两条通道

zh-CN/concepts/tools.title: 工具体系
zh-CN/concepts/tools.summary: 工具从注册、被选中、分发到结果落地的完整链路，以及并行度、超时、预算和裁剪口径。

zh-CN/concepts/core-realtime.title: 实时性
zh-CN/concepts/core-realtime.summary: 执行过程持续可见：WebSocket 是唯一实时通道，断线用游标补水补齐，客户端看到的始终是后端真相的投影，慢客户端会被保护性脱钩。

headings.text: 后端是真相，前端是投影
展示读取是有界分页的

zh-CN/concepts/core-stability.title: 稳定性
zh-CN/concepts/core-stability.summary: 出错不扩散、失败能恢复、问题可复盘。稳定性来自四类硬约束——有界、预算、熔断、单写者——以及出错后统一的错误结构与清楚的处置动作。

headings.text: 队列都有界，满了就报忙

zh-CN/concepts/core-observability.title: 可观测性
zh-CN/concepts/core-observability.summary: 日志、运行时指标、监控与线程轨迹、性能与压测四类入口各自的覆盖范围，以及从错误信息出发的排障顺序。

zh-CN/concepts/workspaces.title: 工作区与工作目录
zh-CN/concepts/workspaces.summary: 每个用户有且只有一个工作区，工具以它为根；蛹里是本机上的持久目录，舰体部署时是服务端按用户划分的唯一目录。

zh-CN/concepts/sessions-and-rounds.title: 会话与轮次
zh-CN/concepts/sessions-and-rounds.summary: 对话的编号方式：线程、用户轮次、模型轮次、时间线条目，以及权威的计数口径。

zh-CN/concepts/streaming.title: 流式执行
zh-CN/concepts/streaming.summary: 执行过程实时到达界面的路径：先落库再推送、按游标续传、前端只消费有界视图。

zh-CN/concepts/presence-and-runtime.title: 运行时与在线状态
zh-CN/concepts/presence-and-runtime.summary: 会话不只是静态历史，还带着运行时状态：正在执行、等待审批、等一个输入……这些状态表示会话当前在做什么。

zh-CN/concepts/prompt-and-skills.title: 提示词与技能
zh-CN/concepts/prompt-and-skills.summary: 系统提示词决定智能体的"人格"，技能是它在某类任务里的具体做法。

headings.text: 提示词、技能、记忆各管一段
模板、技能与模型的组合

zh-CN/concepts/memory.title: 长期记忆
zh-CN/concepts/memory.summary: 智能体「记住」你的偏好、背景和长期资料：结构化记忆在对话开始时注入一次，运行中按需补充检索。

headings.text: 初始化注入 vs 运行期检索
记忆和知识库不是一回事

zh-CN/concepts/quota-and-token-usage.title: 额度与 Token 用量
zh-CN/concepts/quota-and-token-usage.summary: 每次模型请求消耗 1 额度，每天发放 1000；Token 用量只用于观测，不参与扣减。

zh-CN/concepts/goal-mode.title: 目标态
zh-CN/concepts/goal-mode.summary: 目标态是按模型轮次预算驱动的会话级持久目标：设定一次，智能体就自动接着做，直到完成、受阻或预算用尽。

zh-CN/concepts/companion.title: 形象系统
zh-CN/concepts/companion.summary: 形象是挂在智能体上的视觉陪伴层：ZIP 形象包 + 精灵表动画，跟着运行状态换动画行，不参与任何执行逻辑。

zh-CN/concepts/boundary-handling.title: 边界处理

en/index.title: wunder
en/index.summary: wunder is an agent orchestration platform. The Pupa is the local AI workbench on your computer, the Beehive is the cloud workbench in a browser, the Helm is the terminal entry point, and the Hull is the shared management platform for teams.

You want the entry point to the whole manual

en/start/quickstart.title: Quick Start

en/start/desktop.title: Starting with the Pupa (Desktop)
en/start/desktop.summary: wunder's default way to work: a local AI workbench. Download, install, open, go — no Hull to deploy first; it calls the engine natively in-process, takes no port, and routes through no HTTP/WebSocket relay.

en/start/server.title: Deploying the Hull (Server)
en/start/server.summary: An optional form. The user-and-agent management platform for multi-user sharing: multi-tenancy, permission governance, channel integration, and agent-app publishing. Once the Hull is up, the Bridge (18000) is served on the same port, and the Beehive is delivered by a separate web-service container (18001).

en/start/cli.title: Using the Helm (CLI)
en/start/cli.summary: The manual local entry point. In a terminal it opens an interactive session; in a pipeline it degrades to a one-shot run. The full set of 22 slash commands, an exec --json event stream, and the complete cloud subcommand family; scheduled tasks and engine queueing are off on the Helm.

en/tools/panels.title: Plan Panel / Question Panel / Sessions Yield
en/tools/panels.summary: Three interaction-control tools: maintaining a visible execution plan, asking the user for a route before acting, and yielding the current turn to wait for an external event.

en/tools/workspace-files.title: Workspace Files
en/tools/workspace-files.summary: Browsing the workspace, searching content, reading files, and writing files.

en/tools/exec.title: Execute Command
en/tools/exec.summary: Run shell commands, compile, test, or call an existing command-line tool; it supports previews, resource budgets, and output guards.

en/tools/skill-call.title: Skill Call
en/tools/skill-call.summary: Loading a skill's instructions and its directory into the current conversation so the agent can work through that skill's process.

en/tools/web-fetch.title: Web Fetch
en/tools/web-fetch.summary: Letting the agent read the body of a web page, for looking things up, reading docs, or inspecting API responses.

en/tools/browser.title: Browser Tools
en/tools/browser.summary: The browser is not a single tool: once enabled it registers a group of `browser_*` tools for opening pages, clicking, typing, waiting, taking screenshots, and reading rendered content.

en/tools/desktop-control.title: Desktop Control
en/tools/desktop-control.summary: In desktop mode, the Desktop Controller and Desktop Monitor drive the local mouse and keyboard, capture screenshots, and feed the picture to the model as appended visual input.

en/tools/read-image.title: Read Image
en/tools/read-image.summary: Send a local image, animated GIF, or video into the current conversation so the agent can look at the material directly.

en/tools/subagent-control.title: Subagent Control
en/tools/subagent-control.summary: Letting the main agent hand a self-contained piece of work to subagents, then track, wait on, guide, and reclaim them.

en/tools/thread-control.title: Thread Control
en/tools/thread-control.summary: Letting the agent move several things forward at once: create, switch, rename, archive, and restore task threads.

en/tools/self-status.title: Self Status
en/tools/self-status.summary: Checks the current session's model, context usage, round progress, and event counts, for deciding whether to compress context or wrap up.

en/tools/memory-manager.title: Memory Manager
en/tools/memory-manager.summary: Manage the current agent's long-term memory fragments under the current user: list, search, read, add, update, and remove, along with the "short index injection plus fetch-on-demand" pattern.

en/tools/schedule-task.title: Schedule Task
en/tools/schedule-task.summary: Creates, changes, inspects, runs right away, and enables or disables scheduled jobs.

headings.text: Recurring jobs do not pile up

en/surfaces/index.title: Interface Overview
en/surfaces/index.summary: Four forms, four interfaces — the Pupa (local AI workbench), the Beehive (cloud AI workbench), the Helm (terminal interface), and the Bridge (admin governance console). Look up interface capabilities by form.

en/surfaces/frontend.title: Beehive Interface
en/surfaces/frontend.summary: The Beehive is the cloud AI workbench, provided with the Hull deployment and reached in a browser. Its settings include tools, memory, channels, scheduled tasks, devices, and archive; it supports two-way voice (TTS included) and has no interactive terminal.

en/surfaces/web-admin.title: Bridge Interface
en/surfaces/web-admin.summary: The Bridge is the Hull's governance and debugging console. Its top-level navigation has 4 groups and 19 items: System 4, Agents 6, Debug 6, Docs 2.

en/surfaces/desktop-ui.title: Pupa Interface
en/surfaces/desktop-ui.summary: The Pupa (desktop) is the local AI workbench and the default entry for individual users. Its main window has only two pages, chat and settings, with 12 categories in settings; everything else appears as panels and dialogs.

en/capabilities/index.title: Capabilities Overview
en/capabilities/index.summary: Capabilities and operating references: the core capabilities, where a feature lives, what a status means, and how to change a setting.

en/capabilities/api-index.title: Feature and Capability Quick Reference
en/capabilities/api-index.summary: What wunder can do and where each capability lives, organized by feature area.

en/concepts/core-goal.title: Goal
en/concepts/core-goal.summary: The Goal core lets an agent enter goal mode and keep working on one task: three tools drive it, four phases, a default 256-round cap, and automatic blocking after 3 consecutive rounds without progress.

en/concepts/core-compatibility.title: Compatibility
en/concepts/core-compatibility.summary: The Compatibility core lets the Pupa (desktop) and the Helm (cli) run in older operating-system environments under explicit constraints: Windows 7 32-bit and Ubuntu 18.04 each have an offline build chain, and the interface uses software rendering that does not depend on a GPU.

en/concepts/core-context-compression.title: Context Compression
en/concepts/core-context-compression.summary: Long conversations are not cut short when they grow long. The system trims history in graded levels, keeps the most useful information, and lets the conversation continue.

headings.text: What it protects and what it leaves alone

en/concepts/core-subagent.title: Subagents
en/concepts/core-subagent.summary: The Subagents core forks a subtask inside a single thread for an independent executor to complete and return to the parent; the only collaborative form is the subagent, and swarm orchestration has been removed from the engine and the protocol layer.

en/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.title: Scheduled Tasks
en/concepts/core-scheduled-tasks.summary: Scheduled tasks run the agent at a chosen time: three schedule kinds — at for a one-off point, every for a fixed interval, cron for a recurring pattern — with leases, backoff, and auto-disable, so tasks survive a process restart.
read_when: You want a report, inspection, or reminder to run on a schedule instead of by hand
A scheduled task did not run, ran twice, or was disabled on its own
You need to know which forms support scheduling and which do not

headings.text: Where to create one, and support by form

en/concepts/core-channels.title: Channels
en/concepts/core-channels.summary: Feishu, QQ, WeChat, XMPP, and generic webhooks differ in support level; an inbound message is routed to its agent and workspace by binding.

headings.text: A channel is only an entry point
How a message finds its agent and workspace
The boundaries of inbound, outbound, and rate limiting

en/concepts/core-memory.title: Memory
en/concepts/core-memory.summary: Long-term data is injected once when a thread is created and stays frozen afterwards; it has two layers, initialization injection and runtime recall.

headings.text: A few rules that go with it

en/concepts/core-multithreading.title: Multi-threading
en/concepts/core-multithreading.summary: The Multi-threading core raises throughput and resource use through concurrency control inside a single process: one user can hold several concurrent task threads, backed by a session queue, session locks, a parallelism cap, and a daily quota.

en/concepts/core-multi-user-management.title: Multi-user Management
en/concepts/core-multi-user-management.summary: Users, units, and permission boundaries in the Hull (server) form — login state, presence, the unit tree, levels and credits, agent definition documents, and data isolation.
read_when: You are setting up accounts, units, or roles for a Hull deployment
A token, a refresh, or a session on another device behaves unexpectedly
You need to know what Credits measure, and how a worker card differs from a thread

headings.text: The unit tree and the unit-head scope
Levels and credits are two different things
An agent's definition document is not the same thing as a thread

en/capabilities/interlink.title: Interlink
en/capabilities/interlink.summary: The Beehive, the Pupa, and the Helm share one presence state, see each other's workspaces, and control each other in both directions.

en/concepts/architecture.title: Architecture
en/concepts/architecture.summary: All four forms share the same core and engine; real execution happens inside sessions, and the interface reads a bounded display view.

headings.text: Four forms, each with its own delivery surface
What the interface sees is a bounded view, not an execution snapshot

en/concepts/core-agent-loop.title: Agent Loop
en/concepts/core-agent-loop.summary: You state the goal once and the engine runs the remaining steps; the loop advances round by round until it reaches a deliverable result or hits a brake.

headings.text: When it stops on its own
The thread is the unit of execution
When to wait, when to step in, when to open a new thread

en/concepts/core-tools.title: Tools
en/concepts/core-tools.summary: The agent's ability to act comes from a four-layer structure: executor tools, skills that package callable knowledge and scripts, capabilities the administrator selects, and tools the user connects. Keeping the layers distinct is what keeps "selectable" separate from "invokable".

headings.text: Dynamic registration: the model sees more than the built-in list
Result trimming runs on two tracks

en/concepts/tools.title: Tool System
en/concepts/tools.summary: The full path a tool takes from registration and selection through dispatch to its result landing, along with parallelism, timeouts, budgets, and clipping conventions.

headings.text: The path of one tool call

en/concepts/core-realtime.title: Realtime
en/concepts/core-realtime.summary: The realtime channel runs on WebSocket; a reconnect catches up by cursor; what the client sees is a projection of backend truth; slow clients are uncoupled to protect the stream.

headings.text: The backend is truth, the frontend is a projection
Chat streaming runs only over WebSocket
Display reads are bounded and paged

en/concepts/core-stability.title: Stability
en/concepts/core-stability.summary: Errors that do not spread, failures that can recover, and problems that can be reviewed. Stability comes from four kinds of hard constraint — bounds, budgets, circuit breaking, and a single writer — plus a consistent error structure and clear actions when something goes wrong.

headings.text: Every queue is bounded, and a full queue reports busy
Session locks and the single writer
What an error looks like from the outside
Whether to wait or to act

en/concepts/core-observability.title: Observability
en/concepts/core-observability.summary: Where to start looking when something breaks — what logs, runtime metrics and alerts, monitoring and thread traces, and performance testing each tell you, and the order to work through a failure from the error message onward.
read_when: A request, session, or channel failed and you need the first place to look
You need to size log retention, alert thresholds, or a stress test before deploying
You are deciding whether a problem is load, connection, or per-thread behavior

en/concepts/workspaces.title: Workspaces and the Working Directory
en/concepts/workspaces.summary: Each user has exactly one workspace, and tools are rooted at it: a persistent local directory in the Pupa, or a single per-user directory on the server in a Hull deployment.

en/concepts/sessions-and-rounds.title: Sessions and Rounds
en/concepts/sessions-and-rounds.summary: How a conversation is numbered: threads, user rounds, model rounds, timeline entries, and the authoritative counting conventions.

en/concepts/streaming.title: Streaming Execution
en/concepts/streaming.summary: Events are persisted before they are pushed, a reconnect resumes by cursor, and the frontend consumes bounded views.

en/concepts/presence-and-runtime.title: Runtime and Online Status
en/concepts/presence-and-runtime.summary: A conversation is not just static history: it also carries runtime state such as running, waiting for approval, or waiting for input, and that state tells you what the session is doing right now.

headings.text: Where it shows up in the interface

en/concepts/prompt-and-skills.title: Prompts and Skills
en/concepts/prompt-and-skills.summary: The system prompt shapes the agent's persona, and skills are its operating manuals for a class of task.

headings.text: A rule that is easy to trip over
Prompts, skills, and memory each cover their own ground

en/concepts/memory.title: Long-term Memory
en/concepts/memory.summary: How the agent "remembers" your preferences, background, and long-term material—structured memory is injected once when a conversation starts, then supplemented by recall as it runs.

headings.text: Memory and the knowledge base are not the same

en/concepts/quota-and-token-usage.title: Quota and Token Usage
en/concepts/quota-and-token-usage.summary: Each model request costs 1 credit and 1000 are granted daily; token usage is observed only and never deducted.

en/concepts/goal-mode.title: Goal Mode
en/concepts/goal-mode.summary: Goal mode is a session-level persistent goal driven by a model-round budget — set it once, and the agent keeps going on its own until it completes, gets blocked, or spends the budget.

en/concepts/companion.title: Companion System
en/concepts/companion.summary: A companion is a visual layer attached to an agent — a ZIP companion package plus a sprite sheet that follows the runtime state and takes no part in any execution logic.

en/capabilities/config.title: System Settings Reference

en/capabilities/workspace-routing.title: Workspace Routing and File Management
en/capabilities/workspace-routing.summary: Each user has a single cloud workspace directory. Paths are always workspace-relative, and the container parameter has been converged — directories are no longer derived per agent or container.

en/capabilities/mcp-endpoint.title: MCP Endpoint
